_about: The fix catalogue (Claude's design, 2026-10-28): every known way a job or a chat fails, with a pattern a machine can match and the fix that resolves it. Kris edits this. Read by crew/runners/mine_failures.py (which only PROPOSES new entries from real jobs - it never adds one itself) and by the plugin crew/opencode_plugins/fix_commands.js (which rewrites a refused command before it runs) and by pa_build (after-run fixers and the standing rules in a member's brief). Seeded 2026-10-29 by Gordon from Claude's review of the 2026-10-28 failures, so most of these have hits: 1 - the miner corrects the counts.

_kinds.plugin: rewritten BEFORE the call runs (crew/opencode_plugins/fix_commands.js). Only ever drops something the model did not need; never adds, never writes.
_kinds.after_run_hint: nothing is changed for the model - when a build fails its check, the next round's message quotes the compiler's own words for this shape
_kinds.chat_repair: the chat self-repair step (crew/runners/chat_repair.py) fixes the session and resends
_kinds.brief_rule: a fixed standing line in that member's build brief (pa_build's rules), generated ONLY for the members this entry lists, so one member's habits never clutter another's

_statuses.active: match it and act on it
_statuses.record: already fixed at the source; keep counting it so a regression is visible, but do not act

entries.name: drop_stderr_redirect
entries.fixer: plugin: drop the trailing redirection (stderr is captured already)
entries.why: `2>&1` and `2>nul` are matched by the `*>*` deny rule. Harmless to drop: outputs are captured.

entries.name: display_pipe
entries.fixer: plugin: drop the display tail (keep the command before the pipe)
entries.why: These are allowed since afbd34f, so this should no longer fire. Kept because the plugin can drop the tail safely if a member pipes into something else.

entries.name: cmd_exe_syntax
entries.why: The shell is Windows PowerShell (measured from the engine binary: `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command`), so cmd.exe syntax cannot work. Not rewritable safely.
entries.rule: The shell is Windows PowerShell, not cmd.exe. No `dir /s /b`, no `for %f`, no `2>nul`. List files with the glob tool.

entries.name: chained_ampersand
entries.why: PowerShell 5.1 rejects `&` mid-line, and opencode checks each chained part against the allowlist.

entries.name: outside_worktree
entries.why: The build's own rules deny every directory outside its working copy, by design.
entries.rule: Stay in the worktree; it is the whole project. Anything from elsewhere must be quoted in the brief.

entries.name: stale_edit
entries.pattern: has been modified since it was last read
entries.why: Root cause (a formatter rewriting files between read and edit) is off since 2e231b9, but a member can still race itself.
entries.rule: If an edit is refused as stale, read the file again before the next edit. Never repeat the same edit.

entries.name: non_exhaustive_match
entries.why: What the new arm should DO is a decision, not mechanical - so quote the compiler and let the next round decide.
entries.rule: The next round's message lists each missing variant with its file and line.

entries.name: unclosed_delimiter
entries.pattern: error: (this file contains an unclosed delimiter|mismatched closing delimiter)
entries.why: Common in crew-written Rust modules. The compiler gives two locations; both matter.
entries.rule: The next round's message quotes both of the compiler's locations.

entries.name: script_args_split
entries.pattern: attempted relative import with no known parent package
entries.why: Found at the screenshot, not by cargo test - a script path split across arguments. The lesson is that a check needs a smoke run, not only unit tests.
entries.rule: A runtime screenshot or smoke run belongs in the checks for anything with a script argument.

entries.name: bmp_mime
entries.why: Synthetic refuses a BMP; the window writes PNG since 0badd10. Handled by the chat self-repair.

entries.name: engine_password_inherited
entries.why: Fixed at the source: guard.launch drops OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD (8a3e102). Kept so a regression shows up.

entries.name: blind_tool_call
entries.pattern: a tool call answered by an imagined "Tool result" in the same reply
entries.why: A crew-agent failure, not an OpenCode one - already handled in crew/agent.py (e46efb3).
